Layout: a two-way avenue crosses the frame diagonally with a raised median. The far carriageway (F2, 66 tracks) runs right to left, away from the camera; the near carriageway (F1, 73 tracks) runs top-left to bottom-right, towards the camera. Smaller flows: F3 junction centre to bottom-right (10), F4 along the bottom edge right to left (9), F5 right turn from the near carriageway into the bottom-left side street (3). direction_field.json gives the heading per 80 px cell for wrong_way checks.

Signal: a vehicle head on the median at about (2328, 780) and a pedestrian head at (549, 1045) (4K px) can be read from pixel colour. Vehicle phases: red 0 to 34.5 s, green 34.6 to 70.4 s, about 2 s of flashing green, amber 72.5 to 75.4 s, red 75.5 to 114.4 s, green again from 114.5 s. Red and amber show together for about 3 s before each green (31.5 and 111.3 s). Cycle about 80 s. Lamp green explains moving minus stationary vehicles with r = 0.88, so red_light can use the lamp colour directly.

The pedestrian head at (549, 1045) turns green together with the vehicle green (34.4 to 69.5 s), so it most likely serves the side-street crossing at bottom-left, not the crossing of the avenue. This is an inference, not verified.

Stop line, near carriageway: in both red phases the front cars of F1 wait 35 to 41 s at about (1500, 870) and (1764, 985), just before the main zebra (pedestrian band from about (1050, 1300) to (2250, 1100)). On average 5.7 F1 vehicles stand during red vs 1.8 during green.

During the 75 to 115 s red, 4 more cars stand 31 to 39 s inside the junction at x 1544 to 2200, y 1190 to 1375, on or just past the zebra. This may be a second stop line for another approach or vehicles blocking the crossing. Check by eye before building stop_line or failure_to_yield rules on this spot.

Pedestrians are 66% of tracks (541 of 819), 30.7 on screen on average and up to 42. Two crossing corridors carry most road crossings: x 720 to 2240, y 880 to 1600 (59 people) and x 2400 to 3520, y 880 to 1200 (34 people), the two halves of the avenue zebra either side of the median. 14 people are on vehicle lanes outside these corridors, including diagonal walks through the junction near (1550, 1420) and (2250, 1650): jaywalking candidates. The rest are near the far kerb.

Kerbside standing: the far kerb at x 1350 to 1700, y 380 to 520 is a bus stop (4 buses dwell 17 to 25 s) where 2 cars also stand 85 and 97 s, and 3 cars are parked for the whole clip at the left edge (x 50 to 160, y 890 to 1100). stopped_vehicle must whitelist these bays. Queues at the top-left end (x 230 to 500, y 170 to 290) form in both signal phases, so another junction lies beyond the frame.

Person size: median box height is 107 px at 4K (10th percentile 83 px) and grows with image row as h = 0.12 y + 34, from about 80 px at the far kerb to 270 px at the bottom. At imgsz 640 a far pedestrian is about 13 px tall, at 1280 about 27 px, so detection should run at 1280 or on tiles.

Detector ablation on the same video: yolo11m at imgsz 1280 (Kaggle T4) finds 31.6 persons per frame vs 23.0 for yolo11n at 1280 (server CPU), 37% more, and 30% of its person boxes are under 96 px vs 20%, so the gain is mostly small, far pedestrians. It also fragments cars less (211 vs 268 car tracks for the same traffic).

Lighting and tracking caveats: mean luma is only 34 to 54 of 255 and jumps 35% between 52 and 67 s, then falls back around 108 to 122 s. That is too fast for dusk and fits camera auto exposure, so brightness rules (fire_smoke) must normalise per frame. 23% of tracks last under 1 s, and the 2 U-turn-like tracks turn exactly at the right frame edge where F1 exits and F2 enters, so they may be ID switches rather than real U-turns.
